Evidence: 2023 P153 S001-S003 and 2024 P172 S001-S003.

The previous disclosure (D121) details stock-based compensation expense related to Multi-Year Equity Awards. The current disclosure (D130) details stock-based compensation expense related to equity awards assumed in the VMware Merger. While both relate to stock-based compensation, the specific underlying subjects (ongoing multi-year awards vs. merger-assumed awards) are distinct. D121 is a general historical grant expense, whereas D130 is a specific one-time assumption expense. There is no direct textual or thematic link suggesting D121 is the counterpart for the VMware assumption expense. Thus, they are not matched.

comparisons.peer_topic: Share-based compensation expense and tax impacts
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel recognized $3.4 billion in share-based compensation expense in 2024, with associated tax benefits totaling $684 million. Additionally, the company recorded a $139 million tax expense in 2024 due to a shortfall between the tax deduction received and the related deferred tax assets.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC disclose specific dollar amounts for stock-based compensation expense recognized in fiscal year 2024. AVGO reports a total expense of $1,613 million specifically attributed to equity awards assumed in the VMware Merger, while INTC reports a broader share-based compensation expense of $3.4 billion for the same fiscal year. Both disclosures quantify the expense incurred during the period, though AVGO isolates the merger-related component and INTC provides the aggregate recognized amount.
